# S3

Store object metadata in the shared store and object/version/multipart bytes in local files.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `s3` |
| Signing name | `s3` |
| Wire protocol | REST XML |
| API version | `2006-03-01` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Local behavior |
| Selected operations | 66 of 112 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#s3) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- Lifecycle rules do not expire or transition objects.
- Encryption settings are metadata; objects are not encrypted as an AWS S3 data plane would encrypt them, and writes asking for aws:kms are accepted and stored like AES256 objects (aws:kms:dsse is rejected).
- No website endpoint or general ACL evaluation; resource policies do not govern in-process reads.
- POST form fields other than key, Content-Type, x-amz-meta-*, Object Lock, success_action_* and signature fields (acl, tagging, storage class, encryption, cache headers) return NotImplemented; SigV2 POST signatures are unsupported.
- Generated in-process PutObject/UploadPart byte-slice shapes, in-process reads (e.g. Lambda runtime Object() helper), and console download and preview buffers still buffer bytes in memory.
- Verify-mode SigV4 authentication spools upload payloads to temporary files only when verifying signed hexadecimal or empty payload hashes; UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, supported unsigned-trailer forms (STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER), and usual presigned S3 uploads stream without that spool.
- Signed aws-chunked payloads (STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-*) remain unsupported and return NotImplemented.
- Console uploads are limited to 1 MiB per file; object browsing and management in verify mode require an authenticated root console session; storage.s3_max_object_bytes defaults to 256 MiB and can be set up to 5 GiB for object PUTs, parts and completed multipart objects.
- Bucket logging is configuration only: access logs are not generated or delivered; target grants are stored metadata without ACL enforcement.
- GetObjectAttributes omits ObjectParts for nonmultipart objects and objects completed before part metadata was retained; SSE-C is unsupported and its request members are rejected.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
